Pretty broad question, but what's life like in Zimbabwe?

It really depends on who you are referring to as there is a definite "class" system in place here. And the brutal economic conditions translates into "all those who can leave to better pastures have already left" leaving all those that are either ludicrously wealthy/moderately wealthy and living an exceptional lifestyle, or the tiny middle class and the gigantic poor class that both can't escape due to little to no education or simply no wealth to go.

Everyday items like bread, milk, tea, coffee, etc are items that cannot just be purchased in a shop, most of the time you have to visit multiple suppliers to obtain one item. Most people who have moderate wealth simply import all non-perishables and source local perishables via connections you build over time. For the locals without access to wealth, this means 5-hour queues for bread, sugar, cash (i know insane), etc.

If you are in the below 80% of the population, times are brutal, 80%+ unemployment means the youth haven't got a hope in hell of making a life for themselves, education is down the drain so no hope of getting something that can get you into another country or start a business etc apart from a small stall selling vegetables. Quite a few of this proportion tend to be subsistence farmers who live off the land. At the moment these substance farmers have been brutally hit by the prolonged drought that has ravaged crops and killed off tribal cattle and the UN has called for about $2bill US to provide drought relief. In times past the white farmers built reservoirs, boreholes, irrigation channels for surrounding villages in close proximity to the farmers land. Now that these farmers have been dispossessed and infrastructure left to fallow or stolen there is no safeguard for when the rains fail.

If you are among the top 10% life is pretty good, holidays to local game reserves and fishing trips are standard with the occasional overseas trip or intra-continental holidays, large houses with 3+ rooms on 2-4 Acre properties with a swimming pool and a tennis court with at least 2 maids and 2 gardeners. Private schools are a must if you have wealth as state schools are almost non-existent or are simply extremely dilapidated and underfunded. Public healthcare is the same, almost non-existent so private healthcare is also a must. The list goes on and on.

The top 5% are absolutely ludicrously rich and tend to either be wealthy business owners or ultra corrupt government/government ad hoc people who embezzle vast amounts of money or get government "favour ship" for the remainder of whatever government facilities or contracts are left. At any rate both enjoy mansions, latest Mercedes, multiple houses, many foreign holidays, and probably completely imported food, etc.

There are, of course variants between the three groupings but generally, everyone falls quite snugly into one of them.

It is difficult to really describe in text what it is like over there.

But as I have mentioned in other questions the country is brimming with untapped wealth from mineral reserves (platinum, gold, 2nd largest Chrome deposits globally, etc), 70% of the land is near perfect farming land which just needs ,moderate irrigation potential to thrive, the people are very hard working due to the culture (only recently has extreme activity been prevalent but you can't blame the people with the hardship they have been under for decades).

But, on the whole, as long as you own an active business, have a generator for the 5 day week 15-hour power cuts, a borehole for water as the water supplies are erratic, and connections for everyday things like bread, etc life is wonderful. The weather is gorgeous, always sunny and warm.

Life used to be so good for everyone until Robert and kin destroyed the country for petty revenge. When the agricultural sector fell the industrial and commercial sectors which were reliant on materials simply folded overnight and no new business are opening due to a new government mandate for all business over USD $100k must be 51% black Zimbabwean owned, so foreign investment is completely off the table now.

Mining is still moderately active but this is because of large multinationals keeping them running via political/Bribery connections. A decent description of the country would be something to describe in-person so I hope this is enough of a picture to imagine.

I may be biased though but I think my description is quite accurate.
